exec.thesis: Numerai the company is working: AUM 10x'd in three years ($60M → $700M, targeting $1B), JPMorgan committed $500M of capacity, the fund printed +25.45% net with a 2.75 Sharpe in 2024, and a Nov '25 Series C marked the equity at $500M. Numeraire the token is a claim on none of it except by managerial grace — fund fees flow to equity, while the token gets staking demand, slow burns (3.3% of supply in nine years), and ad hoc treasury buybacks ($3.2M in 12 months) that are recycled back out as tournament payouts. The market has already run this experiment: the JPMorgan announcement spiked NMR +140% intraday to $19.55, and it round-tripped entirely — the market will instantly pay for fund-token linkage, and won't pay for hope. Meanwhile the token's microstructure is deteriorating: Binance delisted pairs twice in 2026, volume fell ~44%, and aggregate ±2% depth is ~$250K per side on a $63M market cap. The single lever that changes everything — a formalized fee-linked buyback policy — is entirely in Richard Craib's hands, and until it exists NMR is optionality, not an investment.
own: The only liquid exposure to a JPMorgan-validated AI quant fund scaling toward $1B AUM — token FDV $96M vs. a $500M equity mark set by sophisticated investors (endowments, Paul Tudor Jones) in Nov '25.

Hard-capped, structurally shrinking supply: minting keys burned in 2018 (no inflation possible ever), 3.3% of max supply burned via losing stakes, ~16% of float locked as tournament collateral, and $3.2M of company buybacks in 12 months ≈ 5% of market cap.

A real, decade-deep moat: obfuscated data + stake-weighted meta model + 30,000+ participants with skin in the game — none of it replicable by forking a token, and now being extended to agentic-AI submissions (Numerai MCP).
avoid: Structural value-capture gap: 1%/20% fund economics (≈$27M+/yr gross at $700M AUM, est.) accrue to equity; the token's buybacks exist to refill the payout treasury, not to return capital. The Aug '25 JPM spike-and-round-trip is the market's verdict on this gap.

Liquidity is decaying, not growing: Binance delisted NMR/BTC+ETH pairs (Jan '26) then the USDC pair (Aug 21 '26); volume fell ~44%; ±2% book depth is ~$250K/side — a $1M market order moves price >10%, and there is no perp market for hedged execution.
The USDC staking option (targeted Jul '26) directly erodes the token's core utility: if new stakers prefer USDC collateral, NMR loses its main structural demand leg while keeping all its illiquidity.
questions: Does Craib formalize a fee-linked buyback/burn policy (vs. ad hoc treasury refills)? This is the single re-rating lever — watch blog language and buyback cadence.
What share of staking flows to USDC vs. NMR once the non-NMR rail is live? High USDC adoption hollows out the token thesis.
Does Binance fully delist NMR, and does any major venue offset it? Liquidity is now thin enough that venue decisions dominate price.
When does AUM cross $1B (guided ~late 2026), and does the fund's 2025/2026 performance hold up under the larger book?

biz.narrative: Numerai runs a weekly ML tournament: ~30,000+ data scientists submit stock predictions on obfuscated data, optionally staking NMR on their models. The Stake-Weighted Meta Model blends staked submissions into one signal traded by Numerai One, a long-short global equity hedge fund (1% management / 20% performance fees, $700M AUM as of Jul '26, >$1B/month traded). Winning stakes earn NMR from a fixed treasury (supply is fully minted — payouts are never inflationary); losing stakes are permanently burned. The company replenishes the treasury with open-market buybacks via Coinbase Institutional ($1M Jul '25, $1M Feb '26 at avg $8.57, $1.2M Jul '26). Products beyond the main tournament: Signals (external data), Crypto (launched Jun '24), a residual-volatility tournament, and Numerai MCP for agentic-AI submissions. The critical asymmetry: fund economics accrue to Numerai's equity ($500M Series C mark), not the token — the token's cash-flow linkage is discretionary.

flow.label: To equity / opco — NOT the token

notes: Payout run-rate ($0.2-0.5M/mo) is a third-party estimate — Numerai doesn't publish it; buybacks are company-confirmed. Net treasury flow is roughly balanced at current cadence: buybacks ≈ payouts.

Treasury holds ~3.1M NMR (~28% of max supply) — the dominant holder; a ~3M reserve is earmarked/locked until 2028. Reconciliation between 'locked reserve' and 'operating treasury' is imperfect across sources (flagged).
Fund performance: 2024 +25.45% net, 2.75 Sharpe (best year); 2023 ~-17% drawdown; 2025 full-year figure not publicly located — LP-only disclosure.
Craib publicly disputed CMC's $4M TVL figure (claims ~$20M) — the company actively manages the token narrative but has not changed token policy.

moat.note: Community + obfuscated-data flywheel (10 years of labeled meta-model history) and institutional brand (JPM, PTJ, endowments) are genuinely strong. Token-market liquidity is the glaring weakness (2/5 and falling post-delistings). Regulatory: no SEC action ever filed, but the 2017-era 'is it a security' overhang influenced the 2018 decentralization and still shapes venue decisions.

liquidity.summary: Aggregate ±2% depth is only ~$240K ask / ~$255K bid across ~52 venues against ~$4.4M ADV — among the thinnest books of any $60M+ mcap token, and thinning: Binance pair delistings (Jan + Aug '26) cut activity ~44%. A $250K market order clears the ±2% band; $1M+ moves price >10%. No perp market exists for hedged execution — everything above ~$100K should be worked as TWAP, and exit capacity is the position risk.

tech.narrative: Numerai's stack is a data-and-incentives machine rather than a chain: obfuscated/encrypted equity features (participants model data they cannot interpret or steal), a Stake-Weighted Meta Model that ensembles thousands of staked predictions, and a live fund executing the blend across 30 global markets. The moat compounds through labeled history — ten years of knowing which anonymous modelers are persistently skillful. 2026 infrastructure shifts: 'Atomic Blockchain Staking' moves stakes on-chain (main tournament migration ~Jun '26), a USDC staking rail was targeted for Jul '26, and Numerai MCP opens submissions to AI agents. Embedded bull assumption: crowdsourced, staked ensembles keep beating internal quant desks as AI commoditizes signal generation. Embedded risk: the same commoditization lets competitors replicate crowdsourcing without a token — and Numerai itself just built a stake rail that doesn't need NMR.

devs.title: USDC staking rail
devs.body: The most consequential token development in years, and it's double-edged by design: better for tournament growth (no crypto-volatility deterrent for quants), directly corrosive to NMR staking demand. Watch the stake-mix data before anything else.

devs.title: Agentic AI submissions (Numerai MCP + Skills)
devs.body: AI agents submitting models could 10x participation and meta-model quality without headcount — the strongest fundamental tailwind for the fund (and only indirectly for the token).

devs.title: LLM commoditization of alpha
devs.body: Cuts both ways: floods Numerai with better submissions, but also lets WorldQuant-style platforms and internal desks replicate crowdsourcing cheaply. Numerai's counter is its labeled-history data moat, not the token.

devs.title: Fee-linked token policy
devs.body: Nothing technical prevents routing a fixed share of fund economics to systematic buybacks/burns. It's a policy choice sitting with one founder. Every other item on this page is noise next to this one.

near: NumerCon 2027 — historically where token news lands
catalysts.mid: Three things matter over 12-36 months. First, policy: any shift from ad hoc buybacks toward a stated, fee-linked cadence converts NMR from loyalty token to quasi-equity — the entire bull case compressed into one announcement. Second, the staking mix: if NMR keeps majority share of tournament collateral despite the USDC rail, the utility floor holds; if not, it doesn't. Third, fund compounding: $1B+ AUM with 2024-quality returns makes the buyback budget trivially expandable ($27M+ gross fee pool vs. a $63M token mcap — the company could half-turn the float in two years if it chose to). The bear structural path: full Binance exit plus USDC staking dominance leaves an illiquid token with no mechanical demand — a delisting spiral where the fund thrives while its token dies.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.body: Craib formalizes fee-linked buybacks at $1B+ AUM (even 15-20% of gross fees ≈ $4-6M/yr systematic bid vs. $63M mcap), NMR holds staking majority, supply keeps shrinking. The Aug '25 spike showed the market instantly pays $19+ for this linkage.
scenarios.trip: Tripwires: policy language in blog/NumerCon · buyback cadence tightens to quarterly · AUM >$1B · NMR stake share >60%

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.body: Status quo: ad hoc buybacks roughly offset payouts, price tracks crypto beta with fund-news spikes that fade. Dead money punctuated by tradeable 40-140% event pops.
scenarios.trip: Tripwires: buybacks continue ~2/yr · volume stabilizes >$4M/day · staked NMR holds >1M

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.body: Full Binance delisting + USDC staking dominance hollow out utility; buybacks lapse; liquidity spiral. The fund keeps succeeding — the token just stops being how anyone participates.
scenarios.trip: Tripwires: NMR stake share <40% · buyback gap >8mo · full Binance delist · volume <$2M/day

variant: Both consensus camps are wrong in opposite directions. Crypto-native consensus dismisses NMR as a 2017 relic with no fee share — ignoring that supply mechanics (hard cap, burns, 16% staked, 5%-of-mcap buyback pace) already make it one of the tightest-float tokens extant, attached to a business compounding at venture rates. Fan consensus treats every AUM milestone as bullish — ignoring that the Aug '25 JPM spike round-tripped precisely because fund success doesn't mechanically reach the token. The variant: the binding constraint is POLICY, not performance, and policy has been drifting token-positive for a year (three buybacks, 'NMR is essential to Numerai's future,' on-chain staking migration). The trade is owning the option BEFORE any formalization — signals to monitor are blog language shifts and cadence tightening — while renting, never marrying, the fund-milestone spikes.

methods.name: Token FDV as % of equity mark (10-35%)

valuation.embedded: At $9, the market pays ~20x the company's voluntary buyback pace and gives zero credit for fund growth — rational, given the accrual gap. The reverse-engineered bull requires believing systematic buybacks reach $4-6M/yr against a shrinking float, which requires a policy announcement that costs the company <25% of one year's gross fees. The asymmetry is that the downside (utility erosion) unfolds slowly, while the upside (policy) reprices in a day — the Aug '25 tape is the proof of both speeds.

synthesis: Numerai is the rare crypto project where the underlying business is unambiguously succeeding and the token is unambiguously not capturing it. Supply mechanics are genuinely excellent — hard cap, no vesting, burns, staking lock, buybacks — but they support value rather than create it, and the market prices that correctly at ~20x buyback pace. With ~$250K of ±2% depth, position size IS the risk: even right theses can't exit cleanly. This is an optionality holding, not an allocation — sized so that a -60% bear case is irrelevant and a policy-driven 3x is meaningful.
recText: Recommendation: avoid for size; a small optionality position (well under 1%) is defensible purely on the policy-formalization lever. Enter on liquidity flushes toward $7, not news; sell fund-milestone spikes (they have always round-tripped); reassess everything the day a fee-linked buyback policy — or language pointing at one — appears. Priority follow-ups: NMR-vs-USDC stake mix once the rail is live, and buyback #4 timing vs. the implied 5-6 month cadence.
